literal: General Lou Bo separately led five thousand horse to besiege Fancheng; [4] Feng Yu, Wentong's garrison commander, surrendered the city and more than three thousand households were taken.
idiomatic: Lou Bo led five thousand horse to besiege Fancheng; [4] Feng Yu, Wentong's commander, surrendered the city and more than three thousand households were taken.

literal: On xinsi an edict that Prince of Le'an Fan was to mobilize ten thousand troops of Qin and Yong and build a small city within Chang'an.
idiomatic: On xinsi he ordered Fan, Prince of Le'an, to raise ten thousand men of Qin and Yong and build an inner citadel at Chang'an.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: Feng Chong, King of Liaoxi, submitted a memorial asking to persuade his father to surrender; the Emperor did not consent.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Feng Chong asked leave to persuade his father to submit; the emperor refused.

literal: Ninth month: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute, presenting one trained elephant.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yilong sent tribute, including a trained elephant.

literal: On wuwu an edict that Concurrent Director of Ceremonial Affairs Cui Yi, bearing credentials, was to invest General Who Conquers the Barbarians Yang Nachang as General Who Conquers the South, equal ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and King of Southern Qin.
idiomatic: On wuwu Cui Yi invested Yang Nachang as King of Southern Qin with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Yang Nachang, King of Southern Qin, led his host to besiege Hanzhong.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Yang Nachang, King of Southern Qin, besieged Hanzhong.

literal: Eleventh month, day jiayin: the imperial carriage returned from north of the mountains to the palace.
idiomatic: On jiayin of the eleventh month the court returned from the northern mountains.

literal: Twelfth month, day jisi: general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On jisi of the twelfth month he granted amnesty to the empire.

literal: On xinwei he traveled to north of the Yin Mountains.
idiomatic: On xinwei he went north of the Yin Mountains.

literal: Hong Zu, King of Xiutu in Longxi, led his people inward in submission.
idiomatic: Hong Zu, Xiutu king in Longxi, submitted with his people.

literal: Jin Ya having died, his tribesmen installed his younger cousin from the clan Dangchuan to lead the host.
idiomatic: After Jin Ya died his people set his cousin Dangchuan over them.

literal: An edict that Concurrent Attendant Cadet Lu Xuan was envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: He ordered Lu Xuan, Concurrent Attendant Cadet, to Liu Yilong.

literal: That year Juqu Mengxun died; his son Mujian was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and re-enfeoffed as King of Hexi.
idiomatic: That year Juqu Mengxun died; his son Mujian became General of Chariots and Cavalry and King of Hexi.

literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day yimao: the imperial carriage halted at Nüshui, held a great feast for the ministers, and distributed rewards each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the third year, first month of spring, on yimao the court halted at Nüshui, feasted the ministers, and gave rewards by rank.

literal: On wuxu Feng Wentong sent his Attendant of Affairs Huangmen Attendant Yichen to beg peace; the Emperor did not permit.
idiomatic: On wuxu Wentong sent Yichen to sue for peace; the emperor refused.

literal: On bingchen Jin Dangchuan rebelled.
idiomatic: On bingchen Dangchuan rebelled.

literal: Yang Nachang took Hanzhong and sent seven thousand displaced households of Yong province to Chang'an.
idiomatic: Yang Nachang took Hanzhong and sent seven thousand refugees from Yong to Chang'an.

literal: Second month, day dingmao: Rouran Wuti presented his sister and sent his half-brother Tulu Gui and several hundred attendants with tribute, presenting two thousand horses.
idiomatic: On dingmao of the second month Wuti of the Rouran sent his sister, his half-brother Tulu Gui, and hundreds of attendants with two thousand horses.

literal: On wuyin an edict said: "At the beginning of Our succession the wicked ran wild; the four quarters were not subject; everywhere there was usurpation.
idiomatic: On wuyin an edict said: "When We began to rule, rebels ran wild and the four quarters would not submit."

literal: The Rouran were overbearing north of the desert; the Tiefe ravaged the three Qins.
idiomatic: The Rouran lorded the northern desert; the Tiefe ravaged the three Qins."

literal: Therefore We ate late and forgot sleep, clapped hands and gripped wrists, resolved to sweep away the lingering rebels and bring peace to the myriad realms.
idiomatic: We ate late and slept little, bent on clearing the remnant rebels and pacifying the realm."

literal: Therefore for years campaigns were repeated in the northwest; transport duties wore out the people, agriculture was neglected, flood and drought followed, and rich and poor were unequal—the people did not have enough for household and person; some were cold and poor and could not support themselves—We are deeply grieved.
idiomatic: Years of northwestern war and transport broke the farmers; flood and drought followed; rich and poor diverged and some could not live—We grieve for them."

literal: Now the four quarters follow the track and arms gradually rest; corvée and tax should be eased and the people given respite.
idiomatic: Now the realm is orderly and arms are still; levies should be light and the people rested."

literal: Let provinces, commanderies, and districts assess rich and poor in three grades: the rich pay as usual; the middle are exempt two years; the poorest three years.
idiomatic: Let every district rank wealth in three grades: the rich pay as before, the middle are exempt two years, the poorest three."

literal: Governors and magistrates must strive for fairness and must not curry favor to deceive government.
idiomatic: Governors must be fair and must not flatter to cheat the law."

literal: Proclaim this clearly so all may hear.
idiomatic: Proclaim this until all have heard."

literal: " On xinmao the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On xinmao the court returned to the capital."

literal: Third month, day jiayin: traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: On jiayin of the third month he went to Hexi.

literal: Intercalary month, day jiaxu: King Helian Chang rebelled and fled.
idiomatic: On jiaxu of the intercalary month Helian Chang rebelled and fled.

literal: On bingzi the garrison commander of Hexi killed him.
idiomatic: On bingzi the Hexi garrison killed him.

literal: His plot was verified; all his younger brothers were executed.
idiomatic: The plot proved true; all his brothers were put to death.

literal: On jimao the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On jimao the court returned to the capital.

literal: Duke of Pengcheng Yuan Li was advanced to prince.
idiomatic: Yuan Li, Duke of Pengcheng, was raised to prince.

literal: On xinsi Feng Wentong sent Master of Writing Gao Yong with a memorial declaring himself a vassal; an edict summoned his attendant son.
idiomatic: On xinsi Wentong sent Gao Yong to submit as vassal; the court summoned his heir.

literal: On wuzi Jin Dangchuan led his host to besiege Marquis of Xichuan Peng Wenhui at Yinmi.
idiomatic: On wuzi Dangchuan besieged Peng Wenhui, Marquis of Xichuan, at Yinmi.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day yimao: an edict that General Who Conquers the West, Prince of Changshan Su, was to campaign against Dangchuan.
idiomatic: On yimao of the fourth month of summer he ordered Prince Su of Changshan against Dangchuan.

literal: On dingwei traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: On dingwei he went to Hexi.

literal: On renxu Dangchuan was captured and beheaded at Chang'an as a warning.
idiomatic: On renxu Dangchuan was taken and beheaded at Chang'an.

literal: Sixth month, day jiachen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On jiachen of the sixth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: On xinhai Grand General Who Inspires Awe, Prince of Yongchang Jian, Minister of Works and Duke of Yiyin Changsun Daosheng, and Palace Attendant Gu Bi directed the armies to campaign against Helong.
idiomatic: On xinhai Prince Jian, Changsun Daosheng, and Gu Bi led the armies against Helong.

literal: They cut down the grain.
idiomatic: They destroyed the crops.

literal: They moved the people and returned.
idiomatic: They relocated the people and withdrew.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day xinsi: the Eastern Palace was completed; garrison guards were fully set, one-third of the Western Palace.
idiomatic: On xinsi of the seventh month of autumn the Eastern Palace was finished, with a third of the Western Palace's guard.

literal: On renwu traveled to Meiji and then reached Xicheng.
idiomatic: On renwu he went to Meiji and on to Xicheng.

literal: He ordered the armies to campaign against the Mountain Hu Bai Long in Xihe.
idiomatic: He ordered the armies against Bai Long of the Mountain Hu in Xihe.

literal: Ninth month, day wuzi: he was taken; Bai Long and his commanders were beheaded and the city slaughtered.
idiomatic: On wuzi of the ninth month Bai Long was taken, he and his officers beheaded, and the city sacked.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guisi: the Rouran state sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On guisi of the tenth month of winter the Rouran sent tribute.

literal: On jiawu the remnant band of Bai Long was broken at Wuyuan.
idiomatic: On jiawu Bai Long's remnant was broken at Wuyuan.

literal: An edict that Mountain Hu forced by Bai Long or who came over in surrender were permitted to become commoners.
idiomatic: Mountain Hu coerced by Bai Long or who submitted were made commoners.

literal: Those who shared Bai Long's evil were beheaded by the thousands; their wives and children were taken captive and distributed to the generals each according to merit.
idiomatic: Bai Long's accomplices were beheaded by the thousands; families were taken and given to the troops by merit.

literal: Eleventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiachen: traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: On jiachen of the twelfth month he went to Yunzhong.

literal: Taiyan year 1, spring, first month, day renwu: death penalties and below were each reduced one degree.
idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyan, first month of spring, on renwu capital punishment and below were reduced one degree.

literal: On guiwei palace women of Taizu and Taizong were released to marry.
idiomatic: On guiwei palace women of Taizu and Taizong were freed to marry.

literal: On jiashen general amnesty; the era was changed.
idiomatic: On jiashen he granted amnesty and changed the reign title.

literal: Second month, day gengzi: the Rouran, Yanqi, Cheshi, and other states each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On gengzi of the second month the Rouran, Yanqi, Cheshi, and others sent tribute.

literal: An edict that people of Chang'an and Pingliang moved to the capital who were old and alone and could not support themselves were permitted to return to their native districts.
idiomatic: Those moved from Chang'an and Pingliang who were old and helpless might return home.

literal: On dingwei the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On dingwei the court returned to the capital.

literal: Third month, day renhai: Feng Wentong sent the great general Kezhuo Tong with tribute, excusing himself on his son's illness.
idiomatic: On renhai of the third month Wentong sent Kezhuo Tong with tribute, pleading his son's illness.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengshen: Duke of Yidu Mu Shou was advanced to Prince of Yidu, Duke of Yiyin Changsun Daosheng to Prince of Shangdang, Duke of Yicheng Xi Jin to Prince of Hengnong, Duke of Guangling Lou Fulian to Prince of Guangling—original offices unchanged.
idiomatic: On gengshen of the fifth month Mu Shou, Changsun Daosheng, Xi Jin, and Lou Fulian were raised to princely rank.

literal: Twenty envoys were sent to the Western Regions.
idiomatic: Twenty envoys were sent to the Western Regions.

literal: On jiaxu traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: On jiaxu he went to Yunzhong.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Sixth month, day jiawu: an edict said: "Recently the rebel bandits were eliminated and the frontier tables gradually grew calm; We think to exalt government and spread great rule; therefore We have repeatedly ordered the offices to proclaim favor and put the hundred duties in order.
idiomatic: On jiawu of the sixth month an edict said: "Rebels are gone and the borders calm; We mean to govern well and have often ordered offices to proclaim favor."

literal: The dukes, ministers, teachers, governors, and magistrates may not have fully guided and displayed excellence, causing yin and yang to lose order and harmonious qi to be unbalanced; last spring there was slight drought and eastern tillage did not flourish.
idiomatic: Ministers and magistrates may not have done their part; yin and yang were out of balance; last spring's drought hurt the eastern crops."

literal: We restrained Ourselves in worry and diligence and prayed to the spirits; above and below were all in place.
idiomatic: We disciplined Ourselves and prayed; order was restored above and below."

literal: Could it be that Our sincerity moved them? What a swift response—clouds and rain thundered down and flowing moisture soaked deep.
idiomatic: Perhaps Our sincerity was heard—rain fell at once and soaked the land."

literal: A humble woman brought a square-inch jade seal to the house of Marquis Sun of Lu county; afterward she vanished and none knew where she went.
idiomatic: A woman brought a small jade seal to Marquis Sun of Lu county, then vanished without trace."

literal: The jade was fresh white and shone within.
idiomatic: The stone was bright white and luminous within."

literal: The seal had three characters in dragon-and-bird form, subtle and wondrous beyond human trace, reading 'Drought and plague pacified.'
idiomatic: Three characters in dragon-bird script read, 'Drought and plague pacified.'"

literal: Tracing the reason, it is likely the spirits' response.
idiomatic: This was surely the spirits' answer."

literal: We are pleased by it.
idiomatic: We rejoice at it."

literal: Recently auspicious omens have come again and again: everywhere sweet dew flowed and descended within the halls;
idiomatic: Lately omens have multiplied: sweet dew fell in the halls;"

literal: fine melons grew with joined stems in Zhongshan;
idiomatic: fine melons with joined stems grew in Zhongshan;"

literal: wild trees joined in one trunk in Wei commandery, in the district where the empresses were born;
idiomatic: joined trees grew in Wei commandery, birthplace of the empresses;"

literal: white swallows gathered at the old capital of Shengle and dark birds followed, numbering perhaps a thousand;
idiomatic: white swallows gathered at old Shengle and dark birds followed by the thousand;"

literal: fine grain joined ears for years in Hengnong;
idiomatic: fine grain doubled its ears for years in Hengnong;"

literal: white pheasants and white hares both appeared in Bohai; three white pheasants also gathered at Taizu's temple in Pingyang.
idiomatic: white pheasants and hares appeared in Bohai; three white pheasants gathered at Taizu's temple in Pingyang."

literal: Heaven sends fine gifts—by what virtue shall We repay?
idiomatic: Heaven gives such gifts—what virtue can repay them?"

literal: Therefore We inwardly examine in shock, joy and fear mingled.
idiomatic: We look within in awe, joy and fear together."

literal: Let the realm feast for five days, rites repay the hundred spirits, and governors sacrifice the famous mountains and great rivers within their borders, answering Heaven's intent and seeking blessing.
idiomatic: Let the empire feast five days; officials sacrifice famous mountains and rivers to answer Heaven and seek blessing."

literal: " On bingwu Gaoli and Shanshan each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On bingwu Gaoli and Shanshan sent tribute."

literal: On wushen an edict that General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Leping Pi, and five other generals were to lead forty thousand horse east to campaign against Wentong.
idiomatic: On wushen he ordered Prince Pi of Leping and five generals with forty thousand horse east against Wentong.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: hunted at Yuyang.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he hunted at Yuyang.

literal: On jimao Pi and the others reached Helong, moved six thousand men and women, and returned.
idiomatic: On jimao Pi reached Helong, took six thousand people, and returned.

literal: Eighth month, day bingxu: then traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: On bingxu of the eighth month he went to Hexi.

literal: Sogdiana sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Sogdiana sent tribute.

literal: Ninth month, day jiaxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On jiaxu of the ninth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: An Yuan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, plotted rebellion and was executed.
idiomatic: On guimao of the tenth month of winter An Yuan plotted rebellion and was put to death.

literal: On jiachen traveled to Ding province and halted at Xincheng Palace.
idiomatic: On jiachen he went to Ding and halted at Xincheng Palace.

literal: Eleventh month, day yichou: traveled to Ji province.
idiomatic: On yichou of the eleventh month he went to Ji.

literal: On jisi conducted a hunt at Guangchuan.
idiomatic: On jisi he hunted at Guangchuan.

literal: On bingzi traveled to Ye and sacrificed at the temple of Empress Mi.
idiomatic: On bingzi he went to Ye and sacrificed at Empress Mi's temple.

literal: Wherever he passed he questioned the aged and honored the worthy.
idiomatic: Along the route he questioned the elderly and honored the able.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiashen: an edict said: "To wield the six handles is how the king governs;
idiomatic: On jiashen of the twelfth month an edict said: "The six handles are how a king rules;"

literal: to settle government and judge suits is what the dukes and ministers preserve;
idiomatic: settling suits is for ministers;"

literal: to encourage agriculture and level levies is what those who govern the people must urgently attend;
idiomatic: encouraging farming and fair taxes is for those who rule the people;"

literal: to exhaust effort in the three seasons is what the common people can accomplish.
idiomatic: the people must labor through the seasons."

literal: Each should keep to his division—that is called order; now it is otherwise—how can there be rule?
idiomatic: Each should keep his place—that is order; now it is not—how can there be government?"

literal: Overstepping office and encroaching on another's charge disorders the statutes;
idiomatic: Overstepping office breaks the law;"
